title: Courtroom Analogy: New Perspective on Uncertainty-Aware Classification
claim: A standard evidential model collapses onto one dominant class, while our structured decomposition captures the true ambiguity between two plausible classes.
layout: 2 rows of 4 bar charts; top baseline, bottom ours; shared input image
description: Eight small bar charts in two rows of four. The top row shows the baseline. It has a blurry CIFAR-10 airplane/ship image labeled 'Ground Truth: ship', then the human-annotated class distribution (CIFAR-10H), which splits between airplane and ship. Next are the EDL concentration parameters alpha, with one huge spike on class 0 (airplane), and the EDL predicted mean, which is dominated by airplane. The bottom row shows the proposed MoDEX. It has alpha with two large peaks at classes 0 and 8, then tau (shared evidence/advocacy values, red), omega (plausibility weights, purple) and the predicted mean mu (teal). The mean puts mass on both airplane and ship and matches the human distribution. Each plot has its own color, and the titles use math notation. The eye goes first to the image and the top-row spikes, then down to the bottom row's two-peak plots.
caption: Uncertainty-aware classification results for EDL and MoDEX, both trained on CIFAR-10-LT and evaluated on test input x⋆ with the ground-truth label ship (tail class) and semantic ambiguity with airplane (head class). The top row shows the input image, the human-annotated class distribution from CIFAR-10H, and EDL’s concentration parameters α(x⋆) and predicted mean µ(x⋆). The bottom row shows the courtroom parameters induced by MoDEX, along with the predicted mean µ(x⋆).
abstract: Single-pass uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods for classification represent uncertainty by predicting a tractable distribution over the class probability vector. While existing approaches primarily focus on enhancing the expressiveness of this distribution, they often provide limited insight into how predictive uncertainty is structured and aggregated, resulting in weak interpretability. We introduce the courtroom analogy, which conceptualizes uncertainty-aware classification as a structured debate among class-specific advocates. Each advocate forms a probabilistic opinion, and a final verdict is reached by aggregating these opinions using input-dependent plausibility weights. In this framework, each advocate's opinion is modeled as a Dirichlet distribution whose concentration parameter is decomposed into shared evidence and class-specific advocacy. This yields a structured mixture of Dirichlet distributions with semantically interpretable parameters. To instantiate this formulation, we propose Mixture of Dirichlet EXperts (MoDEX), a single-pass neural architecture that predicts the courtroom parameters, enabling efficient and expressive UQ while explicitly modeling uncertainty aggregation. We demonstrate that MoDEX enjoys strong theoretical properties and achieves state-of-the-art UQ performance across diverse benchmarks, yielding interpretable uncertainty estimates with meaningful semantics.
